transcript:
Header: 2026-12-09 16:00 UTC | Duration: ~42m | Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ethan Park (Redwood SE), Sara Kim (Nexera - Procurement), Liam O'Connor (Nexera - CISO), Priya Nair (Nexera - Legal), Dev Patel (Nexera - SRE)

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hi everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro from our side 

- i'm maya, i'm the account lead, and ethan's our solutions engineer.
[00:07] Ethan Park: hey all, hi, um, thanks for setting this up. we'll run through the MSA/DPA questions, SLA matrix, and then chat about onboarding and benchmarks.
[00:15] Sara Kim: great, thanks. from procurement side i'll be driving approvals, priya is legal, liam is security, and dev is our infra owner.
[00:22] Priya Nair: hi all.
[00:23] Liam O'Connor: hello.
[00:25] Dev Patel: hey.

[00:30] Maya Chen: ok, first item 

- MSA and DPA. last week you sent redlines, we reviewed them with legal, and we compiled a response doc. i'll share the redlined MSA and a short summary after this call. quick note 

- there are three ask areas we flagged: liability cap changes, data residency wording, and audit/cert requirements.
[01:00] Priya Nair: on the liability cap 

- our procurement typically wants a cap at 4x fees or $5M minimum, whichever is higher. your standard MSA has a 1x fee cap, and our legal team is concerned about model hallucinations causing regulatory risk for us.
[01:20] Maya Chen: understood. we typically do 1x for platform contracts but can discuss limited carve-outs. one approach we've offered customers is higher caps for enterprise plans or adding a separate indemnity for regulatory claims tied to data breaches. it's not automatic, we need exec approval but we can present options.
[01:40] Priya Nair: ok, please include that in the redline summary.

[01:45] Ethan Park: i'll jump in on data residency and DPA. Devon 

- sorry, dev 

- your question earlier on where logs and customer content live: for hosted customers data is encrypted at rest, and obfuscated logs are stored in our EU region if requested. we also offer Private deployment (VPC/on-prem) for regulated stores. the DPA has sections for data location and retention; our standard retention for audit logs is 90 days but we can extend for enterprise.
[02:20] Dev Patel: what's the process to get us into a EU-only tenancy? we need all PII to remain within eu.
[02:27] Ethan Park: two options: hosted with region pinning (we pin to a eu region) or private (customer-managed VPC). Pinning requires a committed capacity agreement for predictable throughput; private gives you full network control. which tier are you evaluating?
[02:42] Sara Kim: procurement is leaning toward hosted for speed but we need contractual guarantees for residency and SLA. pricing approvals are tied to committed capacity numbers.

[02:55] Liam O'Connor: KMS 

- we use a customer-managed KMS for keys, we don't want platform-managed keys. our policy needs to support HSM-backed KEKs and rotation policies. does Redwood support CMK/HSM integrations?
[03:10] Ethan Park: yes, we support KMS integrations 

- AWS KMS and GCP KMS, and for private we can integrate with your HSM. we'll need to capture exact cipher/key policies; i'll follow up with the security integrations doc. note: some telemetry keys for runtime may still be pseudonymized, we'll document that.

[03:35] Priya Nair: on the DPA, we have a few standard asks: delete on termination within 30 days, subprocessor list, and right to audit. your DPA lists 120 days 

- can you shorten?
[03:48] Maya Chen: we can usually support a 30-60 day delete window depending on your retention needs. right to audit 

- we typically provide SOC 2 reports and annual attestations; for in

- person audits we go through a redwood-managed process. i know that's sometimes called out as insufficient by legal 

- we can map an audit process and offer additional attestations if necessary.

[04:05] Sara Kim: procurement will need to see SOC2, ISO, and any penetration testing summaries. also your subcontractor list.
[04:12] Maya Chen: absolutely 

- we'll attach SOC 2 Type II and the latest pen test summary. subordinated vendors list also included. link: https://redwood.ai/security (note: link readout may be fuzzy in transcript).

[04:25] Dev Patel: performance SLA 
- we have varied workloads, some near real-time chat, some batch. what's your SLA for p95 latency and uptime?
[04:34] Ethan Park: default hosted SLO is 99.5% availability with p95 latencies depending on model/seq length. for dedicated/reserved capacity we can provide 99.9% availability and tighter latency SLOs. we'll share an SLA matrix with numbers per model family. for mission-critical chat we typically recommend dedicated pools or pinned capacity.
[04:55] Dev Patel: and how do you handle graceful degradation if capacity is constrained 

- fallbacks?
[05:00] Ethan Park: yes, smart routing + automated fallback to compatible model variants, and ephemeral burst capacity if included in the contract. there may be a small quality delta if you fallback to a lower-size model 

- we'll document QoL tradeoffs.

[05:15] Sara Kim: pricing 

- procurement needs committed vs burst pricing buckets and an example TCO for our expected monthly tokens. do you have a pricing sheet?
[05:24] Maya Chen: yes, ethan will share a pricing spreadsheet with committed vs burst, unit per-token breakdown, and discount tiers. we'll also include an example TCO using the workloads you provide.

[05:35] Ethan Park: quick thing on benchmarks 

- to give a reliable estimate we need an example prompt set and token distributions. dev, if you can share two sample workloads (chat + batch) we'll run internal benchmarks and include per-token cost and latency numbers on the pricing sheet.
[05:52] Dev Patel: we can provide that. i'll sanitize and send by monday.

[05:58] [small crosstalk, some background noise]

[06:10] Priya Nair: vendor onboarding 

- we need an onboarding checklist: contact points, security questionnaire, entitlement plan, SSO/SAML setup, SCIM, role-based access.
[06:21] Maya Chen: we have a standard onboarding pack; will include steps for SSO (SAML/SCIM), RBAC, and support SLAs. for SSO we support OIDC and SAML, we'll include a sample metadata file.

[06:35] Liam O'Connor: audit logs 

- we need immutable audit trails for admin actions and request/response logs for investigations. retention should be configurable.
[06:46] Ethan Park: audit logs are available; request/response logs can be enabled per account, with redaction controls. retention configurable under enterprise DPA. note that full request/response retention carries cost and we can include in pricing.

[07:00] Priya Nair: about indemnities 

- we also need clauses for regulatory fines if data processing caused pii leaks.
[07:08] Maya Chen: we'll flag where we can include limited indemnities; many customers have negotiated industry-specific carve-outs. i'll include examples in the redline packet.

[07:20] Sara Kim: timeline 

- procurement needs internal approvals by end of quarter, ideally signed before 12/31. is that feasible?
[07:29] Maya Chen: yes, feasible. we just need to align on redlines and pricing this week, run the benchmark early next week, and have your legal and our legal sync if needed.

[07:40] Ethan Park: operationally, for onboarding we'd propose: week 1 

- sign MSA/DPA and set up SSO; week 2 

- run benchmarks and validate SLA; week 3 

- pilot with dedicated pool if committed.

[07:55] Dev Patel: one more technical: KV cache and session storage 

- for low latency chat we rely on KV cache persistence. what are eviction policies and where are caches stored?
[08:06] Ethan Park: runtime KV caches are memory-optimized on the serving tier; for private deployments they live in your VPC. eviction is LRU with pin options for session affinity. we'll add technical notes to the benchmark doc.

[08:20] [00:08:20 timestamp, mid-call summary pause]

[08:25] Maya Chen: ok quick recap before Qs: we'll send the redlined MSA/DPA with summary; we'll attach SOC2, pen test, subprocessor list; ethan will send SLA matrix and pricing sheet and propose benchmark timelines; dev to share workloads; liam to confirm KMS specifics; priya to surface any legal must-haves.

[08:45] Priya Nair: thanks. two smaller items 

- data breach notification timeline (we require 72 hours) and multi-factor for admin accounts.
[08:55] Maya Chen: 72 hours is consistent with our incident response; MFA for admin is supported and we'll document IDP options.

[09:05] Sara Kim: procurement wants to see a sample statement of work for start of pilot and estimated costs for 3-month pilot.
[09:13] Maya Chen: will do 

- ethan will include in pricing sheet a pilot SOW sample.

[09:20] [background typing]

[09:30] Liam O'Connor: competitors question 

- our security team also looked at LargeCloudAI and OpenServe; how do you compare on isolation and private deployment?
[09:40] Ethan Park: it's a good question. compared to LargeCloudAI we offer dedicated private deployment earlier in the process and more granular observability in the console (per-token traces, audit logs). openserve offers lower price on paper but less integrated rollout tooling. we'll provide a short comparison doc.

[09:58] Dev Patel: ok thanks. we'll evaluate with your benchmark results.

[10:05] Maya Chen: any other questions?

[10:09] Sara Kim: none from procurement.

[10:11] Priya Nair: no but we'll review redlines and likely request a follow-up legal-only call.

[10:16] Liam O'Connor: we might ask for an architecture deep dive but after benchmarks.

[10:22] Maya Chen: great. quick next steps recap: 1) we'll send redlines + summary and security pack (SOC2/pen test/subprocessors) by EOD 12/10; 2) ethan will send SLA matrix + pricing + sample SOW by 12/12; 3) dev shares workloads by 12/13; 4) schedule benchmark early week 12/14-12/16.

[10:44] Sara Kim: procurement will target internal approval by 12/20 and sign by 12/31 if redlines are acceptable.

[10:50] Maya Chen: perfect, we'll aim to hit those dates. thanks everyone.

[10:55] Ethan Park: thanks, bye.

[10:57] Priya Nair: bye.

[10:58] Liam O'Connor: bye.

[11:00] End of recording.

Notes: transcript has occasional transcription errors (names, product names). referenced artifacts: MSA/DPA redlines (will be shared), SLA/pricing spreadsheet (link to be sent), security pack at https://redwood.ai/security.
